main_text.p: & vagi, & stipem emendicantes, vt sunt tuus iste Critopulus, & Zygomala, sed eloquentia, gravitate, honore Ecclesiæ Græcæ florentissimi, & quod magis est, Ecclesia ipsa Græca in suis Ritualibus libris, & expressis verbis largiuntur, & tu audes, quasi legendi nescius sis, affirmare, eos Purgatorium Romanum ignorare, & ritum orandi retinere, vt ex viatoribus fiant spectatores? Opinione Græcorum, iusti ipsi, qui non-dum absolute pœnitentiam egerunt, sed remanet illis aliquid expurgandum, plane viatores sunt. Adhuc enim in tormentis & igne peregrinabundi oberrant, & afflictionibus, & igne spurcitiem, & impietatem peccatorum sefe spoliant; donec de-purgati in peroptatam gloriam introducan-tur. Vide quæ Epistola ad D. Boineburgium digessi. Plura alia sunt, quæ præte-reo, leviter tamen unum tangam. Methodius respondet Theodoræ Imperatrici, quæ rogaverat Patres, vt orarent Deum, vt dimitteret delicta Theophilo marito, quæ ille commiserat pro oppugnatione Imaginum, in vita Michaëlis filij Theophili. Οὔ̓ μὲν οὖν δίκαια ἡ ὀρθόδοξος Ἐκκλησία, καὶ ὁ ταύτης ἐξάρχων Μεθόδιος ἔφασκε διαπονεῖν [?], ἐ δ' ἡμᾶς ἐχρῆν ἀπαναίνεσθαι. Δίκαιον δὲ τῆς ἀρχοῦσι, τὰς ... ἀπιπ-[?]

page.notes: Greek passage is read from a small, cramped scan and is uncertain throughout; words marked [?] are best readings, and the final Greek line is cut off at the foot of the page. The catchword at the bottom right is barely legible. Small dots in the left and right margins are printer's or scanning marks, not text, and are left out. The page has no running head. Possible typographic irregularities in the Latin ("sefe", "leviter") are copied as printed or normalised per u/v rules, as noted.
